(string, error) {\n\tifIndex, err := d.OverwriteNode.CalculateInterfaceIndex(ifName)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", err\n\t}\n\tif ifIndex < d.FirstDataIfIndex {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\"extracted interface index for %q is out of bounds: %d ! >= %d\",\n\t\t\tifName,\n\t\t\tifIndex,\n\t\t\td.FirstDataIfIndex,\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\tmappedIfName := fmt.Sprintf(\"%s%d\", d.InterfaceMappedPrefix, ifIndex)\n\n\treturn mappedIfName, nil\n}\n\n// VerifyStartupConfig verifies that startup config files exists on disks.\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) VerifyStartupConfig(topoDir string) error {\n\tcfg := d.Config().StartupConfig\n\tif cfg == \"\" {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\trcfg := clabutils.ResolvePath(cfg, topoDir)\n\tif !clabutils.FileExists(rcfg) {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q startup-config file not found by the path %s\",\n\t\t\td.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName(), rcfg)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// GenerateConfig generates configuration for the nodes\n// out of the template `t` based on the node configuration and saves the result to dst.\n// If the config file is already present in the node dir we do not regenerate the config unless\n// EnforceStartupConfig is explicitly set to true and startup-config points to a file this will\n// persist the changes that users make to a running config when booted from some startup config.\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) GenerateConfig(dst, t string) error {\n\t// Check for incompatible options\n\tif d.Cfg.EnforceStartupConfig && d.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig {\n\t\treturn ErrIncompatibleOptions\n\t}\n\tif d.Cfg.EnforceStartupConfig && d.Cfg.StartupConfig == \"\" {\n\t\treturn ErrNoStartupConfig\n\t}\n\n\tif d.Cfg.SuppressStartupConfig {\n\t\tlog.Info(\"Startup config generation suppressed\", \"node\", d.Cfg.ShortName)\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tif !d.Cfg.EnforceStartupConfig && clabutils.FileExists(dst) {\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Existing config found\", \"node\", d.Cfg.ShortName, \"path\", dst)\n\t\treturn nil\n\t} else {\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Generating config\", \"node\", d.Cfg.ShortName, \"file\", d.Cfg.StartupConfig)\n\n\t\tcfgBuf, err := clabutils.SubstituteEnvsAndTemplate(strings.NewReader(t), d.Cfg)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Generated config\", \"node\", d.Cfg.ShortName, \"content\", cfgBuf.String())\n\n\t\tf, err := os.Create(dst)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tdefer f.Close()\n\n\t\t_, err = f.Write(cfgBuf.Bytes())\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// NodeOverwrites is an interface that every node implements.\n// It is used to enable DefaultNode to get access to the particular node structs\n// and is provided as an argument of the NewDefaultNode function.\n// The methods defined for this interfaces are the methods that particular node has a custom\n// implementation of.\ntype NodeOverwrites interface {\n\tVerifyStartupConfig(topoDir string) error\n\tCheckInterfaceName() error\n\tGetImages(ctx context.Context) map[string]string\n\tGetContainers(ctx context.Context) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error)\n\tGetContainerName() string\n\tGetContainerStatus(ctx context.Context) clabruntime.ContainerStatus\n\tVerifyContainerName() error\n\tVerifyLicenseFileExists(context.Context) error\n\tPreStop(context.Context) error\n\tRunExec(context.Context, *clabexec.ExecCmd) (*clabexec.ExecResult, error)\n\tGetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error)\n}\n\n// LoadStartupConfigFileVr templates a startup-config using the file specified for VM-based nodes in\n// the topo\n// and puts the resulting config file by the LabDir/configDirName/startupCfgFName path.\nfunc LoadStartupConfigFileVr(node Node, configDirName, startupCfgFName string) error {\n\tnodeCfg := node.Config()\n\t// create config directory that will be bind mounted to vrnetlab container at / path\n\tclabutils.CreateDirectory(path.Join(nodeCfg.LabDir, configDirName),\n\t\tclabconstants.PermissionsOpen)\n\n\tif nodeCfg.StartupConfig != \"\" {\n\t\t// dstCfg is a path to a file on the clab host that will have rendered configuration\n\t\tdstCfg := filepath.Join(nodeCfg.LabDir, configDirName, startupCfgFName)\n\n\t\tc, err := os.ReadFile(nodeCfg.StartupConfig)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tcfgTemplate := string(c)\n\n\t\terr = node.GenerateConfig(dstCfg, cfgTemplate)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tlog.Errorf(\"node=%s, failed to generate config: %v\", nodeCfg.ShortName, err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// GetContainerName returns the name used by the runtime to identify the container\n// e.g. ext-container nodes use the name as defined in the topo file, while most other containers\n// use long (prefixed) name.\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) GetContainerName() string {\n\treturn d.Cfg.LongName\n}\n\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) VerifyContainerName() error {\n\tcontainerName := d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName()\n\tif !containerNamePatternRe.MatchString(containerName) {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"Node name contains invalid characters: %s\", containerName)\n\t}\n\n\tif len(containerName) > maxNameLength {\n\t\tlog.Warn(\n\t\t\t\"Node name will not resolve via DNS\",\n\t\t\t\"name\",\n\t\t\tcontainerName,\n\t\t\t\"reason\",\n\t\t\tfmt.Sprintf(\"name exceeds %d characters\", maxNameLength),\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\n\tif strings.ContainsAny(containerName, dnsIncompatibleChars) {\n\t\tlog.Warn(\n\t\t\t\"Node name will not resolve via DNS\",\n\t\t\t\"name\",\n\t\t\tcontainerName,\n\t\t\t\"reason\",\n\t\t\t\"name contains invalid characters such as '.' and/or '_'\",\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// RunExec executes a single nil\n}\n\n// VerifyLicenseFileExists checks if a license file with a provided path exists.\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) VerifyLicenseFileExists(_ context.Context) error {\n\tif d.Config().License == \"\" {\n\t\tswitch d.LicensePolicy {\n\t\t// if a license is required by the kind but not provided\n\t\tcase clabtypes.LicensePolicyRequired:\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"node %s of kind %s requires a license. Provide one via 'license' knob in the topology file\",\n\t\t\t\td.Config().ShortName,\n\t\t\t\td.Cfg.Kind,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\tcase clabtypes.LicensePolicyWarn:\n\t\t\t// just warn when no license is provided\n\t\t\tlog.Warnf(\n\t\t\t\t\"node %s of kind %s requires a license. Make sure to provide it in some way (e.g. license knob or baked into image)\",\n\t\t\t\td.Config().ShortName,\n\t\t\t\td.Cfg.Kind,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\tcase clabtypes.LicensePolicyNone:\n\t\t\t// license is not required\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"unknown license policy value %s for node %s kind %s\",\n\t\t\t\td.LicensePolicy, d.Config().ShortName, d.Cfg.Kind)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// if license is provided check path exists\n\trlic := clabutils.ResolvePath(d.Config().License, d.Cfg.LabDir)\n\tif !clabutils.FileExists(rlic) {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\"license file for node %q is not found by the path %s\",\n\t\t\td.Config().ShortName,\n\t\t\trlic,\n\t\t)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// LoadOrGenerateCertificate loads a certificate using a certificate storage provider\n// provided in certInfra or generates a new one if it does not exist.\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) LoadOrGenerateCertificate(\n\tcertInfra *clabcert.Cert,\n\ttopoName string,\n) (nodeCert *clabcert.Certificate, err error) {\n\t// early return if certificate generation is not required\n\tif d.Cfg.Certificate == nil || !*d.Cfg.Certificate.Issue {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\tnodeConfig := d.Cfg\n\n\t// try loading existing certificates from disk and generate new ones if they do not exist\n\tnodeCert, err = certInfra.LoadNodeCert(nodeConfig.ShortName)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Debugf(\"creating node certificate for %s\", nodeConfig.ShortName)\n\n\t\thosts := []string{\n\t\t\tnodeConfig.ShortName,\n\t\t\tnodeConfig.LongName,\n\t\t\tnodeConfig.ShortName + \".\" + topoName + \".io\",\n\t\t}\n\t\t// add the SANs provided via config\n\t\thosts = append(hosts, nodeConfig.Certificate.SANs...)\n\n\t\t// add mgmt IPs as SANs to CSR\n\t\tfor _, ip := range []string{d.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address, d.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address} {\n\t\t\tif ip != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\thosts = append(hosts, ip)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tcertInput := &clabcert.NodeCSRInput{\n\t\t\tCommonName:   nodeConfig.ShortName + \".\" + topoName + \".io\",\n\t\t\tHosts:        hosts,\n\t\t\tOrganization: \"containerlab\",\n\t\t\tCountry:      \"US\",\n\t\t\tKeySize:      d.Cfg.Certificate.KeySize,\n\t\t\tExpiry:       d.Cfg.Certificate.ValidityDuration,\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Generate the cert for the node\n\t\tnodeCert, err = certInfra.GenerateAndSignNodeCert(certInput)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// persist the cert via certStorage\n\t\terr = certInfra.StoreNodeCert(nodeConfig.ShortName, nodeCert)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn nodeCert, nil\n}\n\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) GetHostsEntries(ctx context.Context) (clabtypes.HostEntries, error) {\n\tcontainers, err := d.OverwriteNode.GetContainers(ctx)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tresult := clabtypes.HostEntries{}\n\n\tfor idx := range containers {\n\t\tif len(containers[idx].Names) == 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif containers[idx].NetworkSettings.IPv4addr != \"\" {\n\t\t\tresult = append(result, clabtypes.NewHostEntry(\n\t\t\t\tcontainers[idx].NetworkSettings.IPv4addr,\n\t\t\t\tcontainers[idx].Names[0],\n\t\t\t\tclabtypes.IpVersionV4,\n\t\t\t).SetDescription(fmt.Sprintf(\"Kind: %s\", d.Cfg.Kind)).SetContainerID(containers[idx].ID))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif containers[idx].NetworkSettings.IPv6addr != \"\" {\n\t\t\tresult = append(result, clabtypes.NewHostEntry(\n\t\t\t\tcontainers[idx].NetworkSettings.IPv6addr,\n\t\t\t\tcontainers[idx].Names[0],\n\t\t\t\tclabtypes.IpVersionV6,\n\t\t\t).SetDescription(fmt.Sprintf(\"Kind: %s\", d.Cfg.Kind)).SetContainerID(containers[idx].ID))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn result, nil\n}\n\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) AddLinkToContainer(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tlink netlink.Link,\n\tf func(ns.NetNS) error,\n) error {\n\tif !d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased {\n\t\tst := d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)\n\t\tif !clabruntime.ContainerHasJoinableNetns(st) {\n\t\t\tif st == clabruntime.Stopped {\n\t\t\t\tcontainerName := d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName()\n\t\t\t\td.GetRuntime().LogNonRunningContainerOutput(ctx, containerName)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"node %q: cannot attach link, container network namespace is not available (status=%s)\",\n\t\t\t\td.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\tst,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// retrieve nodes nspath\n\tnsp, err := d.OverwriteNode.GetNSPath(ctx)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\t// retrieve the namespace handle\n\tnetns, err := ns.GetNS(nsp)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\t// move veth endpoint to namespace\n\tif err := netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(netns.Fd())); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\t// execute the given function\n\terr = netns.Do(f)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// ExecFunction executes the given function in the nodes network namespace.\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) ExecFunction(ctx context.Context, f func(ns.NetNS) error) error {\n\tif d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName()\n\t\t\t\td.GetRuntime().LogNonRunningContainerOutput(ctx, containerName)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\t\"node %q: cannot exec a command, container network namespace is not available (status=%s)\",\n\t\t\t\td.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\tst,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// retrieve nodes nspath\n\tnspath, err := d.OverwriteNode.GetNSPath(ctx)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tif d.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased {\n\t\tnshandle, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\tnspath = nshandle.Path()\n\t}\n\n\tif nspath == \"\" {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"nspath is not set for node %q\", d.GetShortName())\n\t}\n\n\t// retrieve the namespace handle\n\tnetns, err := ns.GetNS(nspath)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\t// execute the given function\n\treturn netns.Do(f)\n}\n\n// AddEndpoint maps the endpoint name to before adding it to the node endpoints if it matches the\n// interface alias regexp. %q could not be mapped: %w\",\n\t\t\t\td.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\te.GetIfaceName(),\n\t\t\t\terr,\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t\tlog.Debugf(\n\t\t\t\"Interface Mapping: Mapping interface %q (ifAlias) to %q = append(d.Endpoints, e)\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) AdoptEndpoint(e clablinks.Endpoint) error {\n\tif e == nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q cannot adopt a nil endpoint\", %q\",\n\t\t\t\td.Cfg.ShortName,\n\t\t\t\te.GetIfaceName(),\n\t\t\t)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\td.Endpoints = append(d.Endpoints, e)\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) ReleaseEndpoint(e d.Runtime.IsHealthy(ctx, d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName())\n}\n\n// ParkEndpoints moves all tracked endpoints into the node-owned parking namespace.\nfunc (d *DefaultNode) ParkEndpoints(ctx context.Context) error {\n\tparkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(d.parkingNetNSName())\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create parking netns for node %q: %w\", d.Cfg.ShortName, err)\n\t}\n\t// Reuse the parking node retained by a failed restore so it keeps the parked endpoints.\n\tparkingNode := d.parkingNode\n\treused := parkingNode != nil\n\tif !reused {\n\t\tparkingNode = clablinks.NewParkingNode(d.Cfg.LongName, parkPath)\n\t}\n\n\tif err := parkingNode.CaptureFrom(ctx, d); err != nil {\n\t\tif !reused {\n\t\t\t_ = d.cleanupParkingNetNS()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tif err := parkingNode.RepointSymlink(); err != nil {\n\t\trepointErr := fmt.Errorf(\"failed to repoint symlink for node %q: %w\", Reasoning
Key observations so far:

1. `VRNode.AddEndpoint`: If `vr.InterfaceRegexp != nil` and the endpoint name does NOT match `VMInterfaceRegexp` (`eth[1-9]\d*$`), it calls `GetMappedInterfaceName`. So for `1/1/1` → maps. For `eth2` etc. matches VMInterfaceRegexp, no mapping. For `eth11`, `eth12` matched. OK.

But note: interface alias `1/1/X` mapping: `InterfaceRegexp = ^1/1/(?P<port>[1-9]|10)$` with offset 1 and FirstDataIfIndex 1 → calculatedIndex = port - 1 + 1 = port. So `1/1/1` → eth1. Good.

2. `CheckInterfaceName` in VRNode checks against `VMInterfaceRegexp` = `eth[1-9]\d*$`. That allows `eth1`-`eth12` but also `eth100`. Help string says 1..12. Not a new issue though—the regexp is shared across all VR nodes. Hmm, but this node has only 12 interfaces; `eth13` would be accepted but not exist on the switch. Other VR nodes accept similarly broad ranges. Not a new defect.

3. `SaveConfig` in vr-vaos.go: uses file-based handshake with the vrnetlab launcher. Interesting concerns:
   - The request file `save` content: `.vaos-save-request` written with "save\n". This must match the launcher's protocol (in vrnetlab repo, external). Can't verify, but this is how the docs describe it.
   - `waitSaveDone`: reads doneFile; empty file means still being written. Race: `os.Remove(doneFile)` at start removes stale done file. If the launcher writes the done file between the clab Remove and ReadFile... fine.
   - Race: request file is written; if a previous save request file was left (e.g., previous save errored and `os.Remove(reqFile)` was called only on error path). On success, the request file isn't removed. The launcher presumably removes it. In the test's fakeLauncher, launcher removes req file. So the launcher removes the request file after consuming. But if the launcher is an older version not supporting save, the req file stays forever, timeout occurs and req removed. OK.
   - Potential race in error path: `waitSaveDone` errors (timeout/ctx) → removes reqFile. But if the launcher is mid-save and reads... whatever.
   - One subtle bug: in `waitSaveDone`, if `os.ReadFile` returns an error, it just continues polling. Fine.
   - Another: on success the reqFile is not removed by clab; relies on launcher. If launcher removed it — fine. But if the launcher already consumed it... Actually the launcher does remove it in the fake. What if the real launcher doesn't remove it? Then a subsequent save would immediately... well, the launcher would see the request file already present and... hmm, actually potential issue: if the request file remains after a successful save (launcher doesn't delete), the next save writes the file again (same content) which is fine; but the launcher may poll for the file's existence and it would already exist... Actually with mtime-based polling it's fine. Can't verify launcher behavior; it's external. Not worth flagging strongly.

4. `Init` in vr-vaos.go — compare with other VR nodes e.g. vr-aoscx. Let me read vr-aoscx.go to compare the pattern (especially `n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, ...)` — dereference assignment. This copies DefaultNode etc. Some nodes do `n.VRNode = ...`? Let's check how other nodes handle. E.g. vr_aoscx.

Also note in vr-vaos.go Init: `n.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf("--username %s --password %s --hostname %s ...")` — credentials passed on the command line visible in `ps`/docker inspect. That's the pattern used by all vrnetlab nodes presumably.

Potential issue: `n.Cfg.Env["USERNAME"]` uses merged env, so a user can override USERNAME/PASSWORD via env; but credentials used by scrapli are `n.Cfg.Credentials` (from topo node user/password or defaults). If the user sets env USERNAME to something different from credentials, mismatch. Existing pattern.

Another: `defEnv` includes `DOCKER_NET_V4_ADDR: n.Mgmt.IPv4Subnet`. Same as others.

5. The `InterfaceHelp` says "1 <= X <= 12" for ethX, but `VMInterfaceRegexp` allows eth13+. Minor.

6. In the test `newTestNode`: sets `n.OverwriteNode = n` but `n.InterfaceMappedPrefix = "eth"` — note it sets fields on the embedded DefaultNode via promotion. Fine.

Wait — in the test, `newTestNode` sets `VRNode: clabnodes.VRNode{...}` directly, bypassing NewVRNode. `VRNode.Credentials` is nil but not needed for these tests.

7. Schema: added `ale_vaos` to the kind enum and a `kind-specific-config` property `ale_vaos` referencing node-config + kind-specific-config-other. Compare to how other VR kinds are represented, e.g. `aruba_aoscx`. Looks consistent. Also check `nodes/kind_specific_config.go` — maybe there's a Go-side validation of kinds for kind-specific config. Let me check whether there's a registry listing which kinds have kind-specific config, and whether there is a "generic_vm"-style list. Also check `nodes/vr_aoscx` to see if aoscx has special handling like `MANAGEMENT_INFO` etc.

8. Docs: `docs/manual/kinds/index.md` table says ALE OmniSwitch vAOS supported VM. Fine.

9. Potential real issue: In `Init`, the bind `fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.ConfigDirName), ":/config")` — uses `path.Join` (URL path) instead of `filepath.Join`; on Windows, LabDir may contain backslashes; `path.Join` won't normalize. Other VR nodes: let me check vr-aoscx to see which they use. If others use path.Join too, it's consistent.

10. SaveConfig handshake: The doc says "`containerlab save` runs `write memory flash-synchro` on each vAOS node and stores the output of `show configuration snapshot` in `clab-<lab_name>/<node_name>/config/startup-config.cfg`". The Go code returns ConfigPath without verifying the file exists/changed. The launcher writes it. OK.

Concern: `SaveConfig` request file written as `0o644` in the config dir which is bind-mounted into the container. Fine.

Concern: If the save is initiated while container is not running (e.g. `containerlab save` on a stopped lab), the request file will never be consumed → timeout after 5 minutes. Does the save command check container health first? Let's check cmd/save.go and how SaveConfig is invoked. Other nodes using scrapli/netconf would also fail. A 5-minute hang per node could be poor UX but not a defect per se. Let's check how `save` handles errors/hang and whether ctx cancellation works (it does via select on ctx.Done).

Actually wait: in `waitSaveDone`, when ctx is done, the select returns ctx.Err() — good. But when ctx has a shorter deadline than saveTimeout, fine.

Another subtle bug in `waitSaveDone`: the poll period check happens AFTER the file read; if the done file never appears, we wait savePollPeriod per iteration — fine.

One more: the timeout check `time.Now().After(deadline)` happens after ReadFile; first iteration: read fails, then check deadline — if timeout is tiny (like the test's 10ms), returns timeout. Fine.

11. Now think about `Init`: `n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)`. NewVRNode sets `vr.InterfaceMappedPrefix = "eth"`, `InterfaceOffset = 0`, etc. Then in Init after that, sets InterfaceOffset=1 and InterfaceHelp. OK.

But note: the struct assignment `n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, ...)` copies the DefaultNode with OverwriteNode = n. Fine — same pattern used elsewhere presumably.

12. Now check `PreDeploy`: VRNode.PreDeploy calls `LoadStartupConfigFileVr(n, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName)`, which creates the config dir. Good — the bind mount points to a dir created in PreDeploy. Wait, does PreDeploy run before container create? Yes.

But wait — `n.ConfigDirName` — is it set? NewVRNode sets `ConfigDirName = "config"` and `StartupCfgFName = "startup-config.cfg"`. In vr-vaos Init, `n.VRNode = *NewVRNode(...)` so those are set. Good.

13. Now let's compare with vr_aoscx to check conventions and find divergences.
Let me compare with an existing VR node and check the save command flow.

1: package core

3: import (

18: func (c *CLab) Save(
19: 	ctx context.Context,
20: 	options ...SaveOption,
21: ) error {
22: 	opts := NewSaveOptions()
23: 	for _, opt := range options {
24: 		opt(opts)
25: 	}
26: 
27: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
28: 		return c.saveWithLabRuntime(ctx, opts)
29: 	}
30: 
31: 	if opts.copyDst != "" {
32: 		resolvedDst, err := c.resolveCopyOutDst(opts.copyDst)
33: 		if err != nil {
34: 			return err
35: 		}
36: 		opts.copyDst = resolvedDst
37: 	}
38: 
39: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
40: 
41: 	wg.Add(len(c.Nodes))
42: 
43: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
44: 		go func(node clabnodes.Node) {
45: 			defer wg.Done()
46: 
47: 			result, err := node.SaveConfig(ctx)
48: 			if err != nil {
49: 				log.Errorf("node %q save failed: %v", node.GetShortName(), err)
50: 				return
51: 			}
52: 
53: 			if opts.copyDst == "" {
54: 				return
55: 			}
56: 
57: 			if err := c.copySavedConfig(ctx, result, node, opts.copyDst); err != nil {
58: 				log.Errorf("node %q save copy failed: %v", node.GetShortName(), err)
59: 			}
60: 		}(node)
61: 	}
62: 
63: 	wg.Wait()
64: 
65: 	return nil
66: }
67: 
68: func (c *CLab) resolveCopyOutDst(dst string) (string, error) {
69: 	baseDir, err := os.Getwd()
70: 	if err != nil || baseDir == "" {
71: 		baseDir = c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileDir()
72: 	}
73: 	if baseDir == "" {
74: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve save dst: current working directory is empty")
75: 	}
76: 
77: 	resolvedDst := clabutils.ResolvePath(dst, baseDir)
78: 	labDir := c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()
79: 	labDirName := filepath.Base(labDir)
80: 	if labDirName == "" || labDirName == "." {
81: 		if c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != "" {
82: 			labDirName = "clab-" + c.Config.Name
83: 		} else {
84: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve save dst: lab directory is empty")
85: 		}
86: 	}
87: 
88: 	dstLabDir := filepath.Join(resolvedDst, labDirName)
89: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(dstLabDir, clabconstants.PermissionsDirDefault); err != nil {
90: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create save dst directory %q: %w", dstLabDir, err)
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	return dstLabDir, nil
94: }
95: 
96: // copySavedConfig copies the saved configuration file from the path in the SaveConfigResult
97: // to the user-specified destination directory with a timestamp in the filename.
98: // A symlink with the original filename is created (or updated) to point to the
99: // latest timestamped copy.
100: //
101: // The destination layout is:
102: //
103: //	<dstRoot>/<nodeName>/config-060102_150405.json   # timestamped copy
104: //	<dstRoot>/<nodeName>/config.json                 # symlink -> timestamped copy
105: func (c *CLab) copySavedConfig(
106: 	ctx context.Context,
107: 	result *clabnodes.SaveConfigResult,
108: 	node clabnodes.Node,
109: 	dstRoot string,
110: ) error {
111: 	if result == nil || result.ConfigPath == "" {
112: 		log.Debug("no saved config path reported, skipping copy", "node", node.GetShortName())
113: 		return nil
114: 	}
115: 
116: 	nodeCfg := node.Config()
117: 	if nodeCfg == nil {
118: 		return fmt.Errorf("node config missing")
119: 	}
120: 
121: 	nodeDstDir := filepath.Join(dstRoot, nodeCfg.ShortName)
122: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(nodeDstDir, clabconstants.PermissionsDirDefault); err != nil {
123: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create save dst node dir %q: %w", nodeDstDir, err)
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	fileName := filepath.Base(result.ConfigPath)
127: 	tsFileName := timestampedFileName(fileName, time.Now())
128: 
129: 	tsPath := filepath.Join(nodeDstDir, tsFileName)
130: 	if err := clabutils.CopyFile(ctx, result.ConfigPath, tsPath,
131: 		clabconstants.PermissionsFileDefault); err != nil {
132: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to copy saved config from %q to %q: %w",
133: 			result.ConfigPath, tsPath, err)
134: 	}
135: 
136: 	// Create or update a symlink with the original filename pointing to the
137: 	// timestamped copy. Remove any existing file/symlink first.
138: 	linkPath := filepath.Join(nodeDstDir, fileName)
139: 	_ = os.Remove(linkPath)
140: 	if err := os.Symlink(tsFileName, linkPath); err != nil {
141: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create symlink %q -> %q: %w", linkPath, tsFileName, err)
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	log.Info(
145: 		"copied saved config",
146: 		"node", nodeCfg.ShortName,
147: 		"src", result.ConfigPath,
148: 		"dst", tsPath,
149: 	)
150: 
151: 	return nil
152: }
153: 
154: // timestampedFileName inserts a timestamp before the file extension.
155: // e.g. "config.json" with ts 2026-02-06 23:59:00 UTC -> "config-260206_235900.json".
156: // Files without an extension get the timestamp appended: "startup-config" ->
157: // "startup-config-260206_235900".
158: func timestampedFileName(name string, t time.Time) string {
159: 	ts := t.UTC().Format("060102_150405")
160: 	ext := filepath.Ext(name)
161: 	base := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ext)
162: 
163: 	return base + "-" + ts + ext
164: }

1: package nodes

12: 
13: // KindSpecificConfigType is a kind's config type, registered with
14: // NodeRegistryEntryAttributes.WithKindSpecificConfig. Only KindSpecificConfigSpec implements it.
15: type KindSpecificConfigType interface {
16: 	newKindSpecificConfig() any
17: }
18: 
19: // KindSpecificConfigSpec binds a kind to its config struct T, which holds the kind-specific keys of
20: // a node
21: // definition. A kind declares one spec, registers it and reads node configs through it:
22: //
23: //	var kindSpecificConfig clabnodes.KindSpecificConfigSpec[KindSpecificConfig]
24: //
25: //	nrea.WithKindSpecificConfig(kindSpecificConfig)
26: //	func (n *iol) kindSpecificCfg() *KindSpecificConfig { return kindSpecificConfig.Of(n.Cfg) }
27: //
28: // T must not implement yaml.Unmarshaler itself; its fields may.
29: type KindSpecificConfigSpec[T any] struct{}
30: 
31: // KindSpecificConfigDefaulter is implemented by kind-specific configs whose defaults are not the
32: // zero value.
33: // Topology keys decode on top of the defaults.
34: type KindSpecificConfigDefaulter interface {
35: 	SetDefaults()
36: }
37: 
38: func (KindSpecificConfigSpec[T]) newKindSpecificConfig() any {
39: 	return newDefaultKindSpecificConfig[T]()
40: }
41: 
42: func newDefaultKindSpecificConfig[T any]() *T {
43: 	t := new(T)
44: 	if d, ok := any(t).(KindSpecificConfigDefaulter); ok {
45: 		d.SetDefaults()
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	return t
49: }
50: 
51: // Of returns cfg's kind-specific config, setting a default T when cfg has none (e.g. a node config
52: // built
53: // outside the topology). A kind-specific config of another type is a programming error and panics.
54: func (KindSpecificConfigSpec[T]) Of(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig) *T {
55: 	switch kc := cfg.KindSpecificConfig.(type) {
56: 	case *T:
57: 		return kc
58: 	case nil:
59: 		t := newDefaultKindSpecificConfig[T]()
60: 		cfg.KindSpecificConfig = t
61: 
62: 		return t
63: 	default:
64: 		panic(
65: 			fmt.Sprintf(
66: 				"node %q: kind-specific config is %T, want %T",
67: 				cfg.ShortName,
68: 				kc,
69: 				(*T)(nil),
70: 			),
71: 		)
72: 	}
73: }
74: 
75: // InvalidKindSpecificConfig stands in for a kind-specific config that failed to decode, e.g. from a
76: // state file written before a key changed. ComputeDiff never considers it equal to another
77: // kind-specific config.
78: type InvalidKindSpecificConfig struct {
79: 	Err string
80: }
81: 
82: // acceptsKey reports whether t has key. Strict decoding of `key: null` fails only for unknown
83: // fields, since yaml.v2 does not call field unmarshalers for null.
84: func acceptsKey(t KindSpecificConfigType, key string) bool {
85: 	b, err := yaml.Marshal(map[string]any{key: nil})
86: 	if err != nil {
87: 		return false
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	return yaml.UnmarshalStrict(b, t.newKindSpecificConfig()) == nil
91: }
92: 
93: var yamlLinePrefix = regexp.MustCompile(`^line \d+: `)
94: 
95: // yamlErrorText returns a yaml.v2 error without its line prefixes, which refer to the
96: // re-marshalled key rather than to the topology file.
97: func yamlErrorText(err error) string {
98: 	var typeErr *yaml.TypeError
99: 	if !errors.As(err, &typeErr) {
100: 		return err.Error()
101: 	}
102: 
103: 	msgs := make([]string, 0, len(typeErr.Errors))
104: 	for _, e := range typeErr.Errors {
105: 		msgs = append(msgs, yamlLinePrefix.ReplaceAllString(e, ""))
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	return strings.Join(msgs, "; ")
109: }
110: 
111: // DecodeKindSpecificConfig strictly decodes a node's raw kind-specific config entries into a new
112: // config of the
113: // kind registered in e. It returns a pointer to the kind's config type, or nil for kinds without
114: // a kind-specific config. Every unsupported key and invalid value is reported, naming the block it
115: // was set
116: // in.
117: func DecodeKindSpecificConfig(
118: 	e *NodeRegistryEntry,
119: 	node, kind string,
120: 	entries []clabtypes.KindSpecificConfigEntry,
121: ) (any, error) {
122: 	t := e.KindSpecificConfigType()
123: 
124: 	var kindSpecificConfig any
125: 	if t != nil {
126: 		kindSpecificConfig = t.newKindSpecificConfig()
127: 	}
128: 
129: 	var errs []error
130: 
131: 	for _, en := range entries {
132: 		if t == nil || !acceptsKey(t, en.Key) {
133: 			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("node %q: kind %q does not support key %q (set in %s)",
134: 				node, kind, en.Key, en.From))
135: 
136: 			continue
137: 		}
138: 
139: 		b, err := yaml.Marshal(map[string]any{en.Key: en.Value})
140: 		if err == nil {
141: 			err = yaml.UnmarshalStrict(b, kindSpecificConfig)
142: 		}
143: 
144: 		if err != nil {
145: 			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("node %q: invalid value for key %q (set in %s): %s",
146: 				node, en.Key, en.From, yamlErrorText(err)))
147: 		}
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	if len(errs) > 0 {
151: 		return nil, errors.Join(errs...)
152: 	}
153: 
154: 	return kindSpecificConfig, nil
155: }

C. `waitSaveDone` race with stale done file: clab removes doneFile before writing request — good ordering: remove done, then write req. If a previous save's done file arrives late (after removal, before new save), the new save could read the *previous* save's result. Sequence: Save1 times out → removes req. 1: # save command
2: 
3: ### Description
4: 
5: The `save` command perform configuration save for all the containers running in a lab.
6: 
7: /// note | Clabernetes runtime
8: With `--runtime c9s`, `save` runs the kind-specific save command in each device
9: container. `save --copy` streams the resulting files back to the local
10: destination using the same copy layout as Docker labs. See
11: [Containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#save) for details.
12: ///
13: 
14: The exact command that performs configuration save depends on a given kind. The below table explains the method used for each kind:
15: 
16: | Kind               | Command                                     | Notes                                                   |
17: | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
18: | **Nokia SR Linux** | `sr_cli -d tools system configuration save` |                                                         |
19: | **Nokia SR OS**    |                                             | delivered via netconf RPC `copy-config running startup` |
20: | **Arista cEOS**    | `Cli -p 15 -c wr`                           |                                                         |
21: | **Juniper cSRX**   | `cli show conf`                             |                                                         |
22: | **Cisco IOL**      | `write memory`                              |                                                         |
23: 
24: --8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
25: 
26: ### Usage
27: 
28: `containerlab [global-flags] save [local-flags]`
29: 
30: ### Flags
31: 
32: #### topology | name
33: 
34: With the global `--topo | -t` flag a user sets the path to the topology definition file that will be used to spin up a lab.
35: 
36: When the topology path refers to a directory, containerlab will look for a file with `.clab.yml` extension in that directory and use it as a topology definition file.
37: 
38: When the topology file flag is omitted, containerlab will try to find the matching file name by looking at the current working directory.
39: 
40: If more than one file is found for directory-based path or when the flag is omitted entirely, containerlab will fail with an error.
41: 
42: Alternatively, use the global `--name` flag to derive the topology from a running lab. This requires the lab to be running and its containers to have the `topo-file` label; otherwise the save command will fail.
43: 
44: #### node-filter
45: 
46: The local `--node-filter` flag allows users to specify a subset of topology nodes targeted by `save` command. The value of this flag is a comma-separated list of node names as they appear in the topology.
47: 
48: When a subset of nodes is specified, containerlab will only attempt to save configuration on the selected nodes.
49: 
50: #### copy
51: 
52: The local `--copy` flag allows users to copy saved configuration files to a dedicated directory. The path is resolved relative to the current working directory unless an absolute path is provided.
53: 
54: When `--copy` is specified, containerlab copies the saved configuration file from its original location in the lab directory to the destination with a UTC timestamp embedded in the filename. A symlink with the original filename is created (or updated) to always point to the latest timestamped copy.
55: 
56: ```
57: <copy-path>/clab-<labname>/<node-name>/<config>-<YYMMDD_HHMMSS>.<ext>   # timestamped copy
58: <copy-path>/clab-<labname>/<node-name>/<config>.<ext>                    # symlink → latest
59: ```
60: 
61: The destination directory is created automatically if it does not exist. Running `save --copy` multiple times to the same directory preserves all previous saves, allowing easy rollback to an earlier configuration.
62: 
63: The exact file that is copied depends on the node kind and corresponds to the configuration file produced by the save operation:
64: 
65: | Kind               | Copied file                                  |
66: | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
67: | **Nokia SR Linux** | `config/config.json`                         |
68: | **Nokia SR OS**    | `<slot>/config/cf3/config.cfg`               |
69: | **Arista cEOS**    | `flash/startup-config`                       |
70: | **Juniper cSRX**   | `config/juniper.conf`                        |
71: 
72: Node kinds that do not report a saved config path are silently skipped.
73: 
74: The `copy` flag opens up the path for saving the running configuration that is used for the startup config. By using the [magic variables](../manual/topo-def-file.md#magic-variables) in the topology file, you can point the startup config to the saved configuration without statically hardcoding the path.  
75: Consider the following lab:
76: 
77: ```yaml
78: name: mylab
79: topology:
80:   nodes:
81:     node1:
82:     node2:
83: ```
84: 
85: After running the lab, save the configuration to a directory:
86: 
87: ```bash
88: containerlab save --copy startup-configs -t mylab.clab.yml
89: ```
90: 
91: The saved configuration will be in the `startup-configs` directory which you can now specify as the startup config for the nodes of the same topology using `__clabLabName__` and `__clabNodeName__` magic variables:
92: 
93: ```yaml
94: name: mylab
95: topology:
96:   nodes:
97:     node1:
98:       startup-config: startup-configs/__clabLabName__/__clabNodeName__/config.json
99:     node2:
100:       startup-config: startup-configs/__clabLabName__/__clabNodeName__/config.json
101: ```
102: 
103: ### Examples
104: 
105: #### Save the configuration of the containers in a specific lab
106: 
107: Save the configuration of the containers running in lab named srl02
108: 
109: ```bash
110: ❯ containerlab save --name srl02
111: INFO[0001] clab-srl02-srl1: stdout: /system:
112:     Generated checkpoint '/etc/opt/srlinux/checkpoint/checkpoint-0.json' with name 'checkpoint-2020-11-18T09:00:54.998Z' and comment ''
113: 
114: INFO[0002] clab-srl02-srl2: stdout: /system:
115:     Generated checkpoint '/etc/opt/srlinux/checkpoint/checkpoint-0.json' with name 'checkpoint-2020-11-18T09:00:56.444Z' and comment ''
116: ```
117: 
118: #### Save and copy configs to a reusable directory
119: 
120: ```bash
121: ❯ containerlab save -t srl02.clab.yml --copy ./startup-configs
122: ```
123: 
124: This creates timestamped copies with symlinks pointing to the latest save:
125: 
126: ```
127: ./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl1/config-260207_091500.json   # timestamped copy
128: ./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl1/config.json                 # symlink → config-260207_091500.json
129: ./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl2/config-260207_091500.json
130: ./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl2/config.json
131: ```
132: 
133: Running the same command again creates new timestamped files and updates the symlinks, while the previous saves remain in the directory.

(End of file - total 133 lines)
</content>

By using the [magic variables](../manual/topo-def-file.md#magic-variables) in the topology file, you can point the startup config to the saved configuration without statically hardcoding the path.  \n75: Consider the following lab:\n76: \n77: ```yaml\n78: name: mylab\n79: topology:\n80:   nodes:\n81:     node1:\n82:     node2:\n83: ```\n84: \n85: After running the lab, save the configuration to a directory:\n86: \n87: ```bash\n88: containerlab save --copy startup-configs -t mylab.clab.yml\n89: ```\n90: \n91: The saved configuration will be in the `startup-configs` directory which you can now specify as the startup config for the nodes of the same topology using `__clabLabName__` and `__clabNodeName__` magic variables:\n92: \n93: ```yaml\n94: name: mylab\n95: topology:\n96:   nodes:\n97:     node1:\n98:       startup-config: startup-configs/__clabLabName__/__clabNodeName__/config.json\n99:     node2:\n100:       startup-config: startup-configs/__clabLabName__/__clabNodeName__/config.json\n101: ```\n102: \n103: ### Examples\n104: \n105: #### Save the configuration of the containers in a specific lab\n106: \n107: Save the configuration of the containers running in lab named srl02\n108: \n109: ```bash\n110: ❯ containerlab save --name srl02\n111: INFO[0001] clab-srl02-srl1: stdout: /system:\n112:     Generated checkpoint '/etc/opt/srlinux/checkpoint/checkpoint-0.json' with name 'checkpoint-2020-11-18T09:00:54.998Z' and comment ''\n113: \n114: INFO[0002] clab-srl02-srl2: stdout: /system:\n115:     Generated checkpoint '/etc/opt/srlinux/checkpoint/checkpoint-0.json' with name 'checkpoint-2020-11-18T09:00:56.444Z' and comment ''\n116: ```\n117: \n118: #### Save and copy configs to a reusable directory\n119: \n120: ```bash\n121: ❯ containerlab save -t srl02.clab.yml --copy ./startup-configs\n122: ```\n123: \n124: This creates timestamped copies with symlinks pointing to the latest save:\n125: \n126: ```\n127: ./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl1/config-260207_091500.json   #         "text": "# save command\n\n### Description\n\nThe `save` command perform configuration save for all the containers running in a lab.\n\n/// note | Clabernetes runtime\nWith `--runtime c9s`, `save` runs the kind-specific save command in each device\ncontainer. `save --copy` streams the resulting files back to the local\ndestination using the same copy layout as Docker labs. See\n[Containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#save) for details.\n///\n\nThe exact command that performs configuration save depends on a given kind. The below table explains the method used for each kind:\n\n| Kind               | Command                                     | Notes                                                   |\n| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **Nokia SR Linux** | `sr_cli -d tools system configuration save` |                                                         |\n| **Nokia SR OS**    |                                             | delivered via netconf RPC `copy-config running startup` |\n| **Arista cEOS**    | `Cli -p 15 -c wr`                           |                                                         |\n| **Juniper cSRX**   | `cli show conf`                             |                                                         |\n| **Cisco IOL**      | `write memory`                              |                                                         |\n\n--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n\n### Usage\n\n`containerlab [global-flags] save [local-flags]`\n\n### Flags\n\n#### topology | name\n\nWith the global `--topo | -t` flag a user sets the path to the topology definition file that will be used to spin up a lab.\n\nWhen the topology path refers to a directory, containerlab will look for a file with `.clab.yml` extension in that directory and use it as a topology definition file.\n\nWhen the topology file flag is omitted, containerlab will try to find the matching file name by looking at the current working directory.\n\nIf more than one file is found for directory-based path or when the flag is omitted entirely, containerlab will fail with an error.\n\nAlternatively, use the global `--name` flag to derive the topology from a running lab. This requires the lab to be running and its containers to have the `topo-file` label; otherwise the save command will fail.\n\n#### node-filter\n\nThe local `--node-filter` flag allows users to specify a subset of topology nodes targeted by `save` command. The value of this flag is a comma-separated list of node names as they appear in the topology.\n\nWhen a subset of nodes is specified, containerlab will only attempt to save configuration on the selected nodes.\n\n#### copy\n\nThe local `--copy` flag allows users to copy saved configuration files to a dedicated directory. The path is resolved relative to the current working directory unless an absolute path is provided.\n\nWhen `--copy` is specified, containerlab copies the saved configuration file from its original location in the lab directory to the destination with a UTC timestamp embedded in the filename. A symlink with the original filename is created (or updated) to always point to the latest timestamped copy.\n\n```\n<copy-path>/clab-<labname>/<node-name>/<config>-<YYMMDD_HHMMSS>.<ext>   # timestamped copy\n<copy-path>/clab-<labname>/<node-name>/<config>.<ext>                    # symlink → latest\n```\n\nThe destination directory is created automatically if it does not exist. Running `save --copy` multiple times to the same directory preserves all previous saves, allowing easy rollback to an earlier configuration.\n\nThe exact file that is copied depends on the node kind and corresponds to the configuration file produced by the save operation:\n\n| Kind               | Copied file                                  |\n| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |\n| **Nokia SR Linux** | `config/config.json`                         |\n| **Nokia SR OS**    | `<slot>/config/cf3/config.cfg`               |\n| **Arista cEOS**    | `flash/startup-config`                       |\n| **Juniper cSRX**   | `config/juniper.conf`                        |\n\nNode kinds that do not report a saved config path are silently skipped.\n\nThe `copy` flag opens up the path for saving the running configuration that is used for the startup config. By using the [magic variables](../manual/topo-def-file.md#magic-variables) in the topology file, you can point the startup config to the saved configuration without statically hardcoding the path.  \nConsider the following lab:\n\n```yaml\nname: mylab\ntopology:\n  nodes:\n    node1:\n    node2:\n```\n\nAfter running the lab, save the configuration to a directory:\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab save --copy startup-configs -t mylab.clab.yml\n```\n\nThe saved configuration will be in the `startup-configs` directory which you can now specify as the startup config for the nodes of the same topology using `__clabLabName__` and `__clabNodeName__` magic variables:\n\n```yaml\nname: mylab\ntopology:\n  nodes:\n    node1:\n      startup-config: startup-configs/__clabLabName__/__clabNodeName__/config.json\n    node2:\n      startup-config: startup-configs/__clabLabName__/__clabNodeName__/config.json\n```\n\n### Examples\n\n#### Save the configuration of the containers in a specific lab\n\nSave the configuration of the containers running in lab named srl02\n\n```bash\n❯ containerlab save --name srl02\nINFO[0001] clab-srl02-srl1: stdout: /system:\n    Generated checkpoint '/etc/opt/srlinux/checkpoint/checkpoint-0.json' with name 'checkpoint-2020-11-18T09:00:54.998Z' and comment ''\n\nINFO[0002] clab-srl02-srl2: stdout: /system:\n    Generated checkpoint '/etc/opt/srlinux/checkpoint/checkpoint-0.json' with name 'checkpoint-2020-11-18T09:00:56.444Z' and comment ''\n```\n\n#### Save and copy configs to a reusable directory\n\n```bash\n❯ containerlab save -t srl02.clab.yml --copy ./startup-configs\n```\n\nThis creates timestamped copies with symlinks pointing to the latest save:\n\n```\n./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl1/config-260207_091500.json   # timestamped copy\n./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl1/config.json                 # symlink → config-260207_091500.json\n./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl2/config-260207_091500.json\n./startup-configs/clab-srl02/srl2/config.json\n```\n\nRunning the same command again creates new timestamped files and updates the symlinks, while the previous saves remain in the directory.",

1: package vr_vaos

3: import (

16: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
17: )
18: 
19: var (
20: 	kindNames = []string{"ale_vaos"}
21: 	// defaultCredentials are the default credentials of the vAOS image.
22: 	defaultCredentials = clabnodes.NewCredentials("admin", "Switch@123")
23: 
24: 	// InterfaceRegexp maps front-panel ports 1/1/1 to 1/1/10 to eth1 to eth10.
25: 	// 1/1/29A and 1/1/30A are only addressable as eth11 and eth12.
26: 	InterfaceRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`^1/1/(?P<port>[1-9]|10)$`)
27: 	InterfaceOffset = 1
28: 	InterfaceHelp   = "1/1/X (where 1 <= X <= 10) or ethX (where 1 <= X <= 12)"
29: )
30: 
31: const (
32: 	// scrapliPlatformName is empty: the vrnetlab launcher handles containerlab save.
33: 	scrapliPlatformName = ""
34: 
35: 	// containerlab save handshake with the vrnetlab launcher, through the
36: 	// config dir mounted at /config in the container.
37: 	saveRequestFile = ".vaos-save-request"
38: 	saveDoneFile    = ".vaos-save-done"
39: 	saveTimeout     = 5 * time.Minute
40: 	savePollPeriod  = time.Second
41: )
42: 
43: // Register registers the node in the NodeRegistry.
44: func Register(r *clabnodes.NodeRegistry) {
45: 	platformAttrs := &clabnodes.PlatformAttrs{
46: 		ScrapliPlatformName: scrapliPlatformName,
47: 	}
48: 
49: 	nrea := clabnodes.NewNodeRegistryEntryAttributes(defaultCredentials, nil, platformAttrs)
50: 
51: 	r.Register(kindNames, func() clabnodes.Node {
52: 		return new(vrVAOS)
53: 	}, nrea)
54: }
55: 
56: type vrVAOS struct {
57: 	clabnodes.VRNode
58: }
59: 
60: func (n *vrVAOS) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...clabnodes.NodeOption) error {
61: 	// Init VRNode
62: 	n.VRNode = *clabnodes.NewVRNode(n, defaultCredentials, scrapliPlatformName)
63: 	// set virtualization requirement
64: 	n.HostRequirements.VirtRequired = true
65: 
66: 	n.Cfg = cfg
67: 	for _, o := range opts {
68: 		o(n)
69: 	}
70: 	// env vars are used to set launch.py arguments in vrnetlab container
71: 	defEnv := map[string]string{
72: 		"CONNECTION_MODE":    clabnodes.VrDefConnMode,
73: 		"USERNAME":           n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
74: 		"PASSWORD":           n.Cfg.Credentials.Password,
75: 		"DOCKER_NET_V4_ADDR": n.Mgmt.IPv4Subnet,
76: 		"DOCKER_NET_V6_ADDR": n.Mgmt.IPv6Subnet,
77: 	}
78: 	n.Cfg.Env = clabutils.MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)
79: 
80: 	// mount config dir to support startup-config functionality
81: 	// (the startup-config is copied to /config/startup-config.cfg and pushed
82: 	// on the console by launch.py once the switch has booted)
83: 	n.Cfg.Binds = append(
84: 		n.Cfg.Binds,
85: 		fmt.Sprint(path.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.ConfigDirName), ":/config"),
86: 	)
87: 
88: 	if n.Cfg.Env["CONNECTION_MODE"] == "macvtap" {
89: 		// mount dev dir to enable macvtap
90: 		n.Cfg.Binds = append(n.Cfg.Binds, "/dev:/dev")
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	n.Cfg.Cmd = fmt.Sprintf(
94: 		"--username %s --password %s --hostname %s --connection-mode %s --trace",
95: 		n.Cfg.Env["USERNAME"],
96: 		n.Cfg.Env["PASSWORD"],
97: 		n.Cfg.ShortName,
98: 		n.Cfg.Env["CONNECTION_MODE"],
99: 	)
100: 
101: 	n.InterfaceRegexp = InterfaceRegexp
102: 	n.InterfaceOffset = InterfaceOffset
103: 	n.InterfaceHelp = InterfaceHelp
104: 
105: 	return nil
106: }
107: 
108: // SaveConfig asks the vrnetlab launcher to save the configuration. The launcher
109: // runs "write memory flash-synchro" on the serial console, writes the output of
110: // "show configuration snapshot" to the startup-config file of the node, then
111: // writes "ok" or the error in the done file.
112: func (n *vrVAOS) SaveConfig(ctx context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
113: 	cfgDir := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.ConfigDirName)
114: 	reqFile := filepath.Join(cfgDir, saveRequestFile)
115: 	doneFile := filepath.Join(cfgDir, saveDoneFile)
116: 
117: 	_ = os.Remove(doneFile)
118: 
119: 	err := os.WriteFile(reqFile, []byte("save\n"), 0o644)
120: 	if err != nil {
121: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: failed to request configuration save: %w",
122: 			n.Cfg.ShortName, err)
123: 	}
124: 
125: 	msg, err := waitSaveDone(ctx, doneFile, saveTimeout)
126: 	if err != nil {
127: 		_ = os.Remove(reqFile)
128: 
129: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", n.Cfg.ShortName, err)
130: 	}
131: 
132: 	if msg != "ok" {
133: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: configuration save failed: %s", n.Cfg.ShortName, msg)
134: 	}
135: 
136: 	configPath := filepath.Join(cfgDir, n.StartupCfgFName)
137: 	log.Info("Saved configuration to path", "nodeName", n.Cfg.ShortName, "path", configPath)
138: 
139: 	return &clabnodes.SaveConfigResult{
140: 		ConfigPath: configPath,
141: 	}, nil
142: }
143: 
144: // waitSaveDone waits for the launcher to write its result in doneFile and
145: // returns it. An empty file is still being written and is read again.
146: func waitSaveDone(ctx context.Context, doneFile string, timeout time.Duration) (string, error) {
147: 	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
148: 
149: 	for {
150: 		b, err := os.ReadFile(doneFile)
151: 		if msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(b)); err == nil && msg != "" {
152: 			_ = os.Remove(doneFile)
153: 
154: 			return msg, nil
155: 		}
156: 
157: 		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
158: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("timeout waiting for the configuration save")
159: 		}
160: 
161: 		select {
162: 		case <-ctx.Done():
163: 			return "", ctx.Err()
164: 		case <-time.After(savePollPeriod):
165: 		}
166: 	}
167: }

Reasoning
Now I have the full picture of the new node. Some observations:

1. `waitSaveDone` timeout check: on the very first iteration, if `os.ReadFile` succeeds with empty content or the file doesn't exist, then checks `time.Now().After(deadline)`. Deadline is now+timeout. With timeout=10ms in the test, the first iteration likely won't trigger; select waits 1s (poll period) since ctx has no Done... wait, `context.Background().Done()` returns nil channel; select with `time.After(1s)` fires after 1s. So the test takes ~1s. Fine.

But consider: if `timeout <= 0` (not realistic), fine.

2. `SaveConfig` writes `"save\n"` to request file. Fine.

3. Empty done file handling: `waitSaveDone` re-reads when msg is empty. Good.

4. Potential issue: `waitSaveDone` reads done file; if ReadFile fails (file doesn't exist), `err != nil` → condition `err == nil && msg != ""` false → continue. Good.

5. `msg != "ok"` — trailing content trimmed. Good.

6. Race with a stale done file from an aborted prior save — my earlier analysis: SaveConfig removes doneFile first, so the only race is if a launcher still processing an earlier request writes the done file between `os.Remove(doneFile)` (line 117) and the launcher's response to the current request. This requires a prior timed-out/cancelled save with a still-running launcher. Low likelihood; P4 hardening note. Actually, hmm — is there a more common scenario? `containerlab save` on a node whose container just started — launcher not yet ready to poll... then request file sits there until launcher starts; timeout at 5 min; clab removes reqFile; but launcher may still see it later (os.Stat then read race — launcher might read the file after clab removed it, WriteFile writes fresh; actually clab removes the req; launcher may have already done open/Stat before removal; then it runs the save, writes done. Then the user runs save again: removes done (present), writes req... launcher for the previous run writes done again → clab reads it as the result of the current save and reports success while the current save never actually happened. Impact: false "saved" state. Rare, requires prior failure + quick retry. I'll report as P4 (hardening), honestly framed. Actually, "prevents data loss" hmm. It's speculative on the launcher protocol (done file could include an id). P4.

7. ethX upper bound: `CheckInterfaceName` in VRNode — need to verify what it does. Let me check vr_node.go CheckInterfaceName. Earlier notes say VMInterfaceRegexp = `eth[1-9]\d*$` allows eth13+. The kind's InterfaceHelp says 1 <= X <= 12, but eth13 passes CheckInterfaceName without error. Let me verify by reading vr_node.go.

168: func preStopPrepareVrnetlabQcowAlias(ctx context.Context, d *DefaultNode) {
169: 	aliasName, ok := vrnetlabQcowAliasName(d.Config().Image)
170: 	if !ok {
171: 		log.Debugf(
172: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias skipped: unable to infer tag from image %q",
173: 			d.Config().ShortName,
174: 			d.Config().Image,
175: 		)
176: 		return
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
180: 	defer cancel()
181: 
182: 	// Some vrnetlab nodes rename the original versioned qcow image after first boot and fail on
183: 	// subsequent starts when they try to rediscover a versioned qcow filename. If there is exactly
184: 	// one non-overlay qcow file in / and our alias is absent, create a hardlink alias based on the
185: 	// image tag.
186: 	cmd := fmt.Sprintf(
187: 		`alias="/%s"; `+
188: 			`[ -e "$alias" ] && exit 0; `+
189: 			`src=""; `+
190: 			`if [ -f /sros.qcow2 ] && [ "/sros.qcow2" != "$alias" ]; then `+
191: 			`src="/sros.qcow2"; `+
192: 			`else `+
193: 			`set -- /*.qcow2; `+
194: 			`if [ "$1" != "/*.qcow2" ]; then `+
195: 			`for f in "$@"; do `+
196: 			`[ "$f" = "$alias" ] && continue; `+
197: 			`base="${f##*/}"; `+
198: 			`case "$base" in *overlay*.qcow2) continue ;; esac; `+
199: 			`if [ -n "$src" ]; then src=""; break; fi; `+
200: 			`src="$f"; `+
201: 			`done; `+
202: 			`fi; `+
203: 			`fi; `+
204: 			`[ -n "$src" ] || exit 0; `+
205: 			`ln "$src" "$alias"`,
206: 		aliasName,
207: 	)
208: 
209: 	execCmd := clabexec.NewExecCmdFromSlice([]string{"sh", "-lc", cmd})
210: 	res, err := d.RunExec(ctx, execCmd)
211: 	if err != nil {
212: 		log.Warnf(
213: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias preparation failed: %v",
214: 			d.Config().ShortName,
215: 			err,
216: 		)
217: 		return
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	if res != nil && res.ReturnCode != 0 {
221: 		log.Warnf(
222: 			"node %q pre-stop vrnetlab qcow alias prep returned code %d (stderr: %s)",
223: 			d.Config().ShortName,
224: 			res.ReturnCode,
225: 			res.Stderr,
226: 		)
227: 	}
228: }

230: func vrnetlabQcowAliasName(image string) (string, bool) {
231: 	tag, ok := imageTag(image)
232: 	if !ok {
233: 		return "", false
234: 	}
235: 
236: 	return "clab-" + tag + ".qcow2", true
237: }
238: 
239: func imageTag(image string) (string, bool) {
240: 	if at := strings.LastIndex(image, "@"); at != -1 {
241: 		image = image[:at]
242: 	}
243: 
244: 	lastSlash := strings.LastIndex(image, "/")
245: 	lastColon := strings.LastIndex(image, ":")
246: 	if lastColon == -1 || lastColon < lastSlash {
247: 		return "", false
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	tag := image[lastColon+1:]
251: 	if tag == "" {
252: 		return "", false
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	if !imageTagRE.MatchString(tag) {
256: 		return "", false
257: 	}
258: 
259: 	return tag, true
260: }

Now I understand the flow:

- `AddEndpoint`: `1/1/1` doesn't match VMInterfaceRegexp → mapped via `GetMappedInterfaceName` using `InterfaceRegexp` + `InterfaceOffset`. `1/1/10` → port=10, mapped to `eth10`. `1/1/11` → regexp fails → error. Good.

This is framework behavior shared by all VR nodes; other nodes' help strings say things like "X >= 1" so they don't over-promise. The vaos help over-promises a bound. This is a P4 doc/behavior mismatch.

8: 
9: [ALE OmniSwitch](https://www.al-enterprise.com/en/products/switches) virtual AOS (vAOS) 8.x is identified with the `ale_vaos` kind in the [topology file](../topo-def-file.md). It is built using the [vrnetlab](../vrnetlab.md) project and essentially is a QEMU VM packaged in a docker container format.
10: 
11: ## Getting the image
12: 
13: To get the vAOS image, contact your ALE representative or ask for it on the [Spacewalkers community](https://www.spacewalkers.com/).
14: 
15: ## Managing ale_vaos nodes
16: 
17: !!!note
18:     Containers with vAOS inside take about 3 minutes to boot and apply their configuration.
19:     You can monitor the progress with `docker logs -f <container-name>`. The node becomes healthy once the bootstrap is done.
20: 
21: === "SSH"
22:     `ssh admin@<container-name>`
23:     Password: `Switch@123`
24: === "Serial console"
25:     `telnet <container-name> 5000`
26: 
27: ## Interface naming
28: 
29: | Container interface | vAOS port |
30: | ------------------- | --------- |
31: | `eth1` to `eth10`   | `1/1/1` to `1/1/10` |
32: | `eth11`             | `1/1/29A` |
33: | `eth12`             | `1/1/30A` |
34: 
35: In the topology, ports `1/1/1` to `1/1/10` can be used directly, for example `os1:1/1/1`. Ports 1/1/29A and 1/1/30A are addressed as `eth11` and `eth12`.
36: 
37: The management interface is the EMP port. With `CLAB_MGMT_PASSTHROUGH: "true"` the EMP port gets the node management address and is bridged to the containerlab management network.
38: 
39: ## Features and options
40: 
41: ### Node configuration
42: 
43: Once the switch has booted, the vrnetlab launcher logs in on the serial console, sets the system name and prompt to the node name, configures the EMP address and saves the configuration.
44: 
45: ### Startup configuration
46: 
47: The [`startup-config`](../nodes.md#startup-config) file is pushed line by line on the serial console after the EMP address is configured, then saved with `write memory flash-synchro`. Use the AOS CLI format of `vcboot.cfg` or `show configuration snapshot`: one command per line, lines starting with `!` are skipped.
48: 
49: ```yaml
50: topology:
51:   nodes:
52:     os1:
53:       kind: ale_vaos
54:       image: vrnetlab/ale_vaos:8.11.162.R01
55:       startup-config: os1.cfg
56: ```
57: 
58: ### Environment variables
59: 
60: | Variable          | Description |
61: | ----------------- | ----------- |
62: | `EMP_ROUTES`      | Static routes on EMP, `prefix=gateway` separated by commas. A default route (0.0.0.0/0) is not allowed on EMP and is skipped. |
63: | `VAOS_EXTRA_CMDS` | Extra CLI commands, separated by `;` |
64: | `VAOS_SAVE`       | `false` skips `write memory flash-synchro` |
65: | `VAOS_BOOTSTRAP`  | `false` skips the console bootstrap |
66: 
67: ### Saving the configuration
68: 
69: `containerlab save` runs `write memory flash-synchro` on each vAOS node and stores the output of `show configuration snapshot` in `clab-<lab_name>/<node_name>/config/startup-config.cfg`.
70: 
71: ## Known issues and limitations
72: 
73: - The node credentials must match an account of the vAOS image (default `admin` / `Switch@123`): they are used by the launcher to log in on the console.
74: - `containerlab save` uses the serial console: close any open console session on the node before saving.

(End of file - total 74 lines)
</content>

  Line 123: Containerlab focuses on the containerized Network Operating Systems which are typically used to test network features and designs. It can also launch traditional virtual machine based routers using [vrnetlab or boxen integration](manual/vrnetlab.md), and it can wire arbitrary linux containers into a lab.


/source/head/docs/manual/nodes.md:
  Line 773: /// note | exec and VM-based (vrnetlab) kinds

  Line 774: For VM-based kinds (vrnetlab integration, e.g. `sonic-vm` and other [VM-based routers](vrnetlab.md)), `exec` runs the command inside the launcher container that wraps the VM, not inside the guest VM itself. The container is only the QEMU wrapper, so guest network-OS commands (e.g. SONiC `show version`) are not on the container's `PATH` and fail with `executable file not found in $PATH`.


/source/head/docs/manual/images.md:
  Line 55: That same `docker tag` command can be used to rename the image so it can be pushed to another registry. For example consider the newly built SR OS 21.2.R1 [vrnetlab](vrnetlab.md) image that by default will have a name of `vrnetlab/vr-sros:21.2.R1`. This container image can't be pushed anywhere in its current form, but retagging will help us out.

  Line 62: sudo docker tag vrnetlab/vr-sros:21.2.R1 ghcr.io/srl-labs/vr-sros:21.2.R1

/source/head/docs/quickstart.md:
  Line 20: In this quickstart we will be using [one of the provided labs](lab-examples/srl-ceos.md) which consists of [Nokia SR Linux](manual/kinds/srl.md) and [Arista cEOS](manual/kinds/ceos.md) nodes connected one to another.

  Line 48: * The nodes are always of a certain [`kind`](manual/kinds/index.md). The `kind` defines the node configuration and behavior.

  Line 49: * Containerlab supports a fixed number of `kinds`. In the example above, the `nokia_srlinux` and `arista_ceos` kinds are used from the [supported catalog](manual/kinds/index.md).

  Line 105: --8<-- "docs/manual/kinds/ceos.md:ceos-get-image"

  Line 163: For example, `nokia_srlinux` kind documentation [provides](manual/kinds/srl.md) the commands to leverage SSH and gNMI interfaces.  

  Line 164: `arista_ceos` kind has its own [instructions](manual/kinds/ceos.md).


/source/head/docs/manual/network.md:
  Line 270: When multiple management networks are defined, every node must have a `mgmt-net` defined (or inherited from groups/kinds/defaults).

  Line 681: It is also possible to interconnect container' data interface not with other container or add it to a [bridge](kinds/bridge.md), but to attach it to a host's root namespace. This is, for example, needed to create a L2 connectivity between containerlab nodes running on different VMs (aka multi-node labs).


/source/head/docs/rn/0.18.md:
  Line 21: Thanks to @log1cb0mb contribution, containerlab now knows how to start [Dell FTOS](../manual/kinds/vr-ftosv.md) systems.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.58.md:
  Line 7: Yes, "IOS on Linux" was a hot thing in early 2000s, but if you don't need datapath features and just want to have a lightweight Cisco IOS - [Cisco IOL](../manual/kinds/cisco_iol.md) is as light as it gets.

  Line 21: And yet another contribution to vrnetlab/containerlab that adds a new system - this time from @rafabr and his work in https://github.com/hellt/vrnetlab/pull/250 that adds [`huawei_vrp`](../manual/kinds/huawei_vrp.md) system.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.35.md:
  Line 28: * added a note on [`et_X_Y`](../manual/kinds/ceos.md#additional-interface-naming-considerations) nameing of ceos.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.78.md:
  Line 42: The new [`ciena_saos`](../manual/kinds/ciena_saos.md) kind adds support for Ciena SAOS 10.x routers as vrnetlab-backed QEMU VMs.

  Line 57: The new [`plvision_sonic`](../manual/kinds/plvision_sonic.md) kind adds PLVision's Enterprise SONiC Linux Distribution as a vrnetlab-backed VM node. Build a containerlab-compatible image from the vendor qcow2 with [vrnetlab](https://github.com/srl-labs/vrnetlab) and wire dataplane ports as `ethN` interfaces.

  Line 104: - The structured [`components`](../manual/kinds/vr-sros.md#components) syntax that SR-SIM introduced in 0.75 now also works with Nokia SR OS vSIM (`nokia_sros`). Thanks @kaelemc #3240


/source/head/docs/rn/0.68.md:
  Line 27: Thanks to @pimvanpelt for populating Containerlab' list of supported nodes with the containerized VPP system. [`fdio_vpp`](../manual/kinds/fdio_vpp.md) is the kind to use to easily build labs run with the VPP nodes.

  Line 31: And if VPP was not enough, please welcome [6Wind VSR](../manual/kinds/6wind_vsr.md) as yet another container-native NOS added to Containerlab. Thanks to @nicoharnois for their contribution!

  Line 35: @takalele added support for [OpenWRT](../manual/kinds/openwrt.md) in #2517. If you always wanted to first try this before flashing your home router with it -- it is a great opportunity!


/source/head/docs/rn/0.45.md:
  Line 7: Thanks to contributions from @akielaries done in #1553 and accompanying vrnetlab PR containerlab gets support for [Juniper vJunos-switch](../manual/kinds/vr-vjunosswitch.md). This is a new VM-based virtual product from Juniper that has been integrated in containerlab by juniper folks, kudos to them!


/source/head/docs/rn/0.46.md:
  Line 76: For example, this is how you can spin up a topology with a single [SR Linux](../manual/kinds/srl.md) node whenver you need it:


/source/head/docs/rn/0.74.md:
  Line 7: The [`spirent_stc`](../manual/kinds/spirent_stc.md) kind adds support for running Spirent containerized Test Center in your labs. The node handles the quirks of STC's cgroups v1 dependency and interface renaming automatically, exposing test ports with `portX` naming that matches the Spirent GUI — so what you see in the topology is what you see in the Spirent interface.

  Line 49: :wave: to the [`veesix_osvbng`](../manual/kinds/veesix_osvbng.md) kind! Containerlab can now run [veesix ::networks](https://github.com/veesix-networks) Open Source vBNG nodes, bringing broadband network gateway functionality to your labs. Packaged as a native container image and available on Docker Hub.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.50.md:
  Line 7: Containerlab now natively supports [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) clusters as part of its topology by introducing a new kind [`k8s-kind`](../manual/kinds/k8s-kind.md).


/source/head/docs/rn/0.11.0.md:
  Line 28: It was possible before with [linux bridges](../manual/kinds/bridge.md), now we are adding support for [ovs bridges](../manual/kinds/ovs-bridge.md) that will allow for even more elaborated and flexible connectivity options.

  Line 57: Support for virtualized EOS from Arista has been added. Now it is possible to use [containerized cEOS](../manual/kinds/ceos.md) and [virtualized vEOS](../manual/kinds/vr-veos.md).

  Line 66: 3. Add [bridge](../manual/kinds/bridge.md) and [linux](../manual/kinds/linux.md) kinds docs.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.13.0.md:
  Line 5: Added support for Cisco CSR1000v system via [`vr-csr`](../manual/kinds/vr-csr.md) kind.

  Line 8: With [`vr-ros`](../manual/kinds/vr-ros.md) kind added support for Mikrotik RouterOS system.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.73.md:
  Line 7: A warm welcome to the [`f5_bigip-ve`](../manual/kinds/f5_bigipve.md) kind! With this addition, Containerlab users can now spin up F5 BIG-IP Virtual Edition appliances as part of their network labs. Built on top of [vrnetlab](../manual/vrnetlab.md), the BIG-IP VE node features management passthrough, day-0 automation for initial configuration and password setup, and configurable resource sizing via environment variables.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.77.md:
  Line 24: The new [`cisco_xrd_vrouter`](../manual/kinds/cisco_xrd_vrouter.md) kind brings Cisco IOS XRd vRouter into containerlab as a vrnetlab-backed micro-VM node. XRd vRouter's dataplane interfaces are PCI-only, so containerlab wires ordinary lab links into emulated NICs presented to the XRd vRouter guest.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.71.md:
  Line 7: For multi component nodes, the config to provision the CPMs, Line cards and MDAs will be [added automatically](../manual/kinds/sros.md#configuration-for-components). This massively simplifies the cognitive load as you no longer need to worry about the essential config to bring up the cards and modules and focus on the actual service configs. Thanks @kaelemc #2827

  Line 23: Thanks to @torbbang, Containerlab got support for Cisco SD-WAN components (vManage, vSmart, vBond). Check [cisco_sdwan kind docs](../manual/kinds/cisco_sdwan.md) for more details. #2877


/source/head/docs/rn/0.47.md:
  Line 21: Containerlab is now able to automatically detect which DNS servers are configured on the hosts and [configure them](../manual/kinds/srl.md#dns-configuration) in the SR Linux'es management VRF accordingly. This aligns SR Linux nodes behavior with the behavior of regular containers launched by Docker where the DNS requests are handled by Docker's DNS resolver #1650.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.36.md:
  Line 11: A new kind - [`cisco_8000`](../manual/kinds/c8000.md) - has been added to the list of supported platforms thanks to an awesome contribution from @rskorka in #1216.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.57.md:
  Line 7: The [Dell SONiC](../manual/kinds/dell_sonic.md) support has been improved by adding startup-config handling and saving #2175


/source/head/docs/rn/0.54.md:
  Line 7: @mzagozen added support for the long-awaited Cisco c8000v router image. Cisco c8000v is a successor of [Cisco CSR1000v](../manual/kinds/vr-csr.md) and is a **different** product from [Cisco 8000](../manual/kinds/c8000.md) platform emulator.

  Line 9: Refer to the [`cisco_c8000v`](../manual/kinds/vr-c8000v.md) kind documentation to learn more about the supported options.

  Line 21: * add `insecure-mgmt` gRPC server to the [default SR Linux config](../manual/kinds/srl.md#grpc-server) #1979


/source/head/docs/rn/0.62.md:
  Line 29: Besides the management network rules, containerlab also sets up rules in the `FORWARD` chain for the [bridge](../manual/kinds/bridge.md) nodes referenced in the topology file. But, again, we missed v6 rules, which are now being added as well (#2401).


/source/head/docs/rn/0.82.md:
  Line 7: Containerlab can now run MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the [official `mikrotik/chr` image](https://hub.docker.com/r/mikrotik/chr) with the [new `mikrotik_chr` kind](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md). The image is used as is - no [vrnetlab](../manual/vrnetlab.md) build - and is published for `amd64` and `arm64`, booting with KVM when `/dev/kvm` is available and falling back to QEMU's TCG emulation otherwise:

  Line 24: The original [`mikrotik_ros`](../manual/kinds/vr-ros.md) kind - CHR from an image built with vrnetlab - is untouched, and both kinds share the interface naming and startup-config conventions, so a lab moves between them by changing `kind` and `image`.

  Line 26: See the [`mikrotik_chr` kind documentation](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md).


/source/head/docs/rn/0.17.md:
  Line 24: A big improvement in the way management interface is configured for [ceos](../manual/kinds/ceos.md) kinds.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.43.md:
  Line 84: Now by specifying the [`host`](../manual/kinds/host.md) node in the topology you can add `exec` section to it and this will tell containerlab to execute commands on the host machine.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.14.0.md:
  Line 15: This allowed for users to, for example, overwrite the `INTFTYPE` env var to allow for using `et` interfaces with cEOS. This is documented in the [ceos kind docs](../manual/kinds/ceos.md).


/source/head/docs/rn/0.30.md:
  Line 12: * management vrf support in ceos with the use of a [`CLAB_MGMT_VRF` env var](../manual/kinds/ceos.md#mgmt-vrf) #941

Built on top of [vrnetlab](../manual/vrnetlab.md), the BIG-IP VE node features management passthrough, day-0 automation for initial configuration and password setup, and configurable resource sizing via environment variables.\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.77.md:\n  Line 24: The new [`cisco_xrd_vrouter`](../manual/kinds/cisco_xrd_vrouter.md) kind brings Cisco IOS XRd vRouter into containerlab as a vrnetlab-backed micro-VM node. XRd vRouter's dataplane interfaces are PCI-only, so containerlab wires ordinary lab links into emulated NICs presented to the XRd vRouter guest.\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.71.md:\n  Line 7: For multi component nodes, the config to provision the CPMs, Line cards and MDAs will be [added automatically](../manual/kinds/sros.md#configuration-for-components). This massively simplifies the cognitive load as you no longer need to worry about the essential config to bring up the cards and modules and focus on the actual service configs. Thanks @kaelemc #2827\n\n  Line 23: Thanks to @torbbang, Containerlab got support for Cisco SD-WAN components (vManage, vSmart, vBond). Check [cisco_sdwan kind docs](../manual/kinds/cisco_sdwan.md) for more details. #2877\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.47.md:\n  Line 21: Containerlab is now able to automatically detect which DNS servers are configured on the hosts and [configure them](../manual/kinds/srl.md#dns-configuration) in the SR Linux'es management VRF accordingly. This aligns SR Linux nodes behavior with the behavior of regular containers launched by Docker where the DNS requests are handled by Docker's DNS resolver #1650.\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.36.md:\n  Line 11: A new kind - [`cisco_8000`](../manual/kinds/c8000.md) - has been added to the list of supported platforms thanks to an awesome contribution from @rskorka in #1216.\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.57.md:\n  Line 7: The [Dell SONiC](../manual/kinds/dell_sonic.md) support has been improved by adding startup-config handling and saving #2175\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.54.md:\n  Line 7: @mzagozen added support for the long-awaited Cisco c8000v router image. Cisco c8000v is a successor of [Cisco CSR1000v](../manual/kinds/vr-csr.md) and is a **different** product from [Cisco 8000](../manual/kinds/c8000.md) platform emulator.\n\n  Line 9: Refer to the [`cisco_c8000v`](../manual/kinds/vr-c8000v.md) kind documentation to learn more about the supported options.\n\n  Line 21: * add `insecure-mgmt` gRPC server to the [default SR Linux config](../manual/kinds/srl.md#grpc-server) #1979\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.62.md:\n  Line 29: Besides the management network rules, containerlab also sets up rules in the `FORWARD` chain for the [bridge](../manual/kinds/bridge.md) nodes referenced in the topology file. But, again, we missed v6 rules, which are now being added as well (#2401).\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.82.md:\n  Line 7: Containerlab can now run MikroTik RouterOS CHR from the [official `mikrotik/chr` image](https://hub.docker.com/r/mikrotik/chr) with the [new `mikrotik_chr` kind](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md). The image is used as is - no [vrnetlab](../manual/vrnetlab.md) build - and is published for `amd64` and `arm64`, booting with KVM when `/dev/kvm` is available and falling back to QEMU's TCG emulation otherwise:\n\n  Line 24: The original [`mikrotik_ros`](../manual/kinds/vr-ros.md) kind - CHR from an image built with vrnetlab - is untouched, and both kinds share the interface naming and startup-config conventions, so a lab moves between them by changing `kind` and `image`.\n\n  Line 26: See the [`mikrotik_chr` kind documentation](../manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md).\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.17.md:\n  Line 24: A big improvement in the way management interface is configured for [ceos](../manual/kinds/ceos.md) kinds.\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.43.md:\n  Line 84: Now by specifying the [`host`](../manual/kinds/host.md) node in the topology you can add `exec` section to it and this will tell containerlab to execute commands on the host machine.\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.14.0.md:\n  Line 15: This allowed for users to, for example, overwrite the `INTFTYPE` env var to allow for using `et` interfaces with cEOS. This is documented in the [ceos kind docs](../manual/kinds/ceos.md).\n\n\n/source/head/docs/rn/0.30.md:\n  Line 12: * management vrf support in ceos with the use of a [`CLAB_MGMT_VRF` env var](../manual/kinds/ceos.md#mgmt-vrf) #941\n\n\n(Results truncated.
